summary.headline: Century Plyboards Q2 FY27 revenue hit record INR1,780 crore (+28.5% YoY); EBITDA ex-forex INR232.3 crore at 13.1% margin, PAT up 46% to INR103.6 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue of INR1,780 crore, with EBITDA excluding forex losses of INR232.3 crore (13.1% margin) and PAT of INR103.6 crore, up 46% YoY. Plywood (+28.6% YoY), laminates (+20.6% YoY), MDF (+10.5% YoY) and particle board (+211% YoY, crossing INR100 crore quarterly revenue) all grew, while logistics reached INR58.8 crore. MDF margins remain depressed by industry overcapacity, with management guiding to double-digit margins only by year-end. Management also said debt has peaked, with net debt to EBITDA at 2.4x in the quarter.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Revenue +28.6% YoY and +14% QoQ with 15.7% EBITDA margin; 7% price hike taken in April contributed to value growth of 30%+. Hoshiarpur 60,000 CBM greenfield plant commissioned, reported at 100% utilisation.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Revenue +20.6% YoY with EBITDA margin up to 11.6%, helped by mix shift away from low-margin liners toward decoratives and compacts. Volumes declined; new Vardhaman press commissioned for large-format products.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue +10.5% YoY and +13.6% QoQ; EBITDA margin ex-forex 8.9%, improved sequentially but still well below the historical ~20% range amid industry overcapacity. Capacity about 6 lakh CBM per year (~INR2,000 crore at current mix).

segments.name: Particle board
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crore quarterly revenue for first time; EBITDA margin ex-forex 7.4% vs 3.7% prior quarter. Capacity 2.4 lakh per annum (~INR600 crore), utilisation below 70% per management, with scope to ~3 lakh via efficiency gains.

segments.name: Logistics (port)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR58.8 crore, +72.7% YoY, nearing EBITDA breakeven in only its second quarter of operation.

guidance_outlook: MDF: 17%-18% volume/revenue growth expected for the full year, with H2 growth similar; management said double-digit EBITDA margin by year-end (H2), not the full year. Margins expected to recover to ~20% from FY29, with FY28 better than FY27.
Laminates: 20%+ revenue growth achievable for the year, with margins expected to improve; revenue, not volume, to be the base metric going forward.

Plywood: EBITDA margin guidance of 14%-15% for FY27 due to planned marketing spend on Total Cover Guarantee campaign; management declined to guide beyond this year, with next-year guidance expected next quarter.
Debt: long-term debt-to-EBITDA target of 1:1, expected to be well below that next year; EBITDA close to INR900 crore projected, with most profit directed to debt repayment.
Enhanced Guwahati and Kandla brownfield plywood capacity expected from July 2027.
risks_watch: MDF overcapacity: ~30% industry capacity addition over the next nine months; margins may stay near 8%-10% until FY29.
Debt: net debt to EBITDA at 2.4x; working capital on a ~60-day cycle; debt repayment depends on sustained EBITDA near INR900 crore.
Plywood margin trajectory as marketing spend rises in Q3-Q4; FY27 guidance of 14%-15% against H1 of 16.3%.
Raw material cost pressure in MDF; dependence on imported core veneer for plywood.
Uncertain timing of the Uttar Pradesh MDF plant (no firm date) and post-FY29 capacity plans.
Laminate volume decline as the company shifts from liners to decoratives and compacts.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and plywood, but cautious on MDF margins, which management expects to stay depressed until overcapacity is absorbed (recovery from FY29). Management was candid on debt and deferred several forward-looking questions (MDF capex date, multi-year guidance).
key_quotes: We achieved our highest-ever quarterly consolidated revenue of INR1,780 crores, registering year-on-year growth of 28.5%.
But right now, pursuing growth aggressively at the cost of margins is something that we do not want to do.
I believe that from FY29 onwards, you will see a substantial recovery in margins.
Long-term debt-to-EBITDA ratio, the target has always been 1:1, and we will be able to maintain that going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why has MDF growth slowed and guidance been trimmed versus peers, and is industry growth slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 MDF growth is double-digit on a high base, but guides 17%-18% for the full year and similar in H2. Industry growth is not the issue; management will not pursue growth at the cost of margins, with raw material cost pressure already visible.

qa_highlights.question: What drives MDF margin recovery to double digits, given overcapacity and the price increase passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified double-digit EBITDA margin is targeted only by year-end (H2), not the full year. Overcapacity from Action and Elixrr means two quarters of consolidation, with gradual recovery next year; visibility is 10% margin in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the UP MDF capex (330,000 CBM, Q2 FY29) still on track, and what is the MDF margin recovery timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm date for the UP MDF plant; land acquisition in progress, and first phase is about 108,000 CBM plywood. Management expects ~30% industry capacity addition over the next nine months, last large addition, with margins recovering from FY29 back toward 20%; FY28 better than FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plywood margin guidance of 14%-15% versus 16.3% in H1: what drives the lower guidance and what is the longer-term view?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikita Bansal said the decline reflects marketing spend on the Total Cover campaign launched in August, with more spend in Q3-Q4. Guidance of 14%-15% is for this year only; management historically gives 13%-15% and prefers to over-perform.

qa_highlights.question: Is plywood volume growth share gain or BIS-driven, and what is sustainable volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About 7% price increase in April drove a large part of the 30%+ value growth. Management credits distribution, brand and stakeholder work; BIS benefit is industry-wide and slow, with about 3,000-4,000 manufacturers yet to comply, and imports stopped. Management declined to guide beyond this year.

qa_highlights.question: Balance sheet: will large capex wait until net debt/EBITDA falls, and what debt level is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is elevated due to recent capex and a 60-day working capital cycle (H1 revenue INR3,300 crore vs INR2,500 crore a year earlier). Long-term debt-to-EBITDA target is 1:1, expected well below that next year; large capex only after this. Management did not commit to a total net debt target. Debt has peaked; EBITDA near INR900 crore projected with most profit going to repayment.

demand_pricing: Consolidated revenue INR1,780 crore, +28.5% YoY; PAT INR103.6 crore, +46% YoY; EBITDA ex-forex INR232.3 crore at 13.1% margin.

Plywood revenue +28.6% YoY and +14% QoQ; value growth of 30%+ partly driven by a 7% price increase taken in April; management attributes volume growth to distribution, brand and stakeholder work. No price hike taken in Q2 in plywood.

Laminates revenue +20.6% YoY; volumes declined as the company shifted from low-realisation liners to decoratives and compacts; revenue to be the base metric going forward. Price hike of about 2%-2.5% taken in Q1 and implemented from November; 7%-8% taken in Q1 per management.

MDF revenue +10.5% YoY and +13.6% QoQ; management says growth is only double-digit in Q2 on a high base, guides 17%-18% for the full year and the same in H2. Industry overcapacity: ~30% capacity addition over the next nine months, with new capacity from Action and Elixrr; raw material cost pressure.
Particle board revenue crossed INR100 crore in a quarter for the first time, +211% YoY and +16.8% QoQ; growth driven by pre-laminated product, which grew faster than plain particle board.
Logistics (port) revenue INR58.8 crore, +72.7% YoY, nearing EBITDA breakeven in its second quarter of operation.
